title: Heat with oil? The evaluators said turn the heat pump off below 8 degrees. A year later, 25.

sentences.text: Heat with oil and own a heat pump? One evaluation's advice: switch the heat pump off on the coldest days and let the oil burner run.

assertions.text: The evaluators recommended that oil-heated homeowners turn off the mini-split in very cold conditions, when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively.
qualifications: s02 gives the thresholds with their years and ties them to that year's prices and the heat pump's cold performance; s04 says this is one evaluation of ductless mini-splits and the advice is for oil-heated homes only.

sentences.text: The switch-off point was 8 degrees Fahrenheit in 2015 and 25 the year after, set by that year's oil and electricity prices and the heat pump's cold performance; dearer oil moves it lower.

assertions.text: The evaluators recommended that oil-heated homeowners turn off the mini-split in very cold conditions, below 8F in 2015 and below 25F in 2016, when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively, depending on energy prices and cold-temperature COPs; if oil prices increase against electric energy rates, the switchover temperature point may move lower.
qualifications: s02 itself ties the thresholds to that year's energy prices and the heat pump's cold performance and says dearer oil moves the point lower; s04 limits them to one evaluation of ductless mini-splits and to oil-heated homes.

sentences.note: L1196-L1201: 'turn off a DMSHP during very cold outdoor conditions (below 8F in 2015 and below 25F in 2016), when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively (depending on energy prices and cold temperature COPs)' and 'If oil prices increase against electric energy rates, the switchover temperature point for oil to DMSHP heat may move lower'. Copied from the parent's s15.a.

sentences.text: That is one evaluation of ductless mini-splits, and the advice is for oil-heated homes only: against propane and electric resistance it found the heat pump cheaper.

assertions.text: In one evaluation of ductless mini-split heat pumps in Massachusetts and Rhode Island homes, the switch-off advice was for oil-heated homes; the same evaluation found mini-splits nearly always less expensive to operate than electric resistance heat and always less expensive than propane heating systems.
qualifications: s04 itself carries the sample (one evaluation of ductless mini-splits) and the scope (oil-heated homes only) beside the propane and resistance results.

sentences.note: L1188-L1190 and L1194-L1195 in the cited passage: 'nearly always be less expensive to operate than electric resistance heat' and 'always operate less expensively than propane heating systems'. The states are the document's population (package documents[].name: MA and RI).

sentences.text: If you heat with oil, ask which heater runs cheaper at this year's prices; the full inquiry asks where a heat pump pays at all.
